categories.main_business_segments: Churchill Downs Incorporated operates three primary business segments: Live and Historical Racing (pari-mutuel wagering on live and historical horse races, simulcast fees, admissions, sponsorships, and food/beverage services), TwinSpires (online horse racing wagering, sports betting, casino gaming, and pari-mutuel wagering systems), and Gaming (casino operations with slot machines, table games, video lottery terminals, and hotel services). The company also owns and operates the iconic Kentucky Derby and manages regional casino properties across multiple states.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes advance deposit wagering (ADW) technology platforms for online horse racing wagering, pari-mutuel wagering systems and totalisator services for race wagering, historical racing machines (HRMs) and slot machine gaming technology, and digital platforms for sports betting and online casino gaming. Churchill Downs operates state-of-the-art facilities including one of the largest 4K video boards in the world at Churchill Downs Racetrack and maintains simulcast and streaming video capabilities for live horse races and replays.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company serves customers interested in horse racing wagering, casino gaming, and sports betting across the United States. Primary customer segments include horse racing enthusiasts, casino patrons, online wagering customers, and sports bettors. Key end markets include Kentucky (Churchill Downs Racetrack and historical racing venues), Virginia (Colonial Downs and Rosie's venues), Pennsylvania, New York, Louisiana, Mississippi, Maine, Maryland, Iowa, and other states where gaming is legalized.
categories.geographic_coverage: Churchill Downs operates in 13 states: Kentucky (Churchill Downs Racetrack, Derby City Gaming, Oak Grove, Turfway Park, Ellis Park), Virginia (Colonial Downs, six Rosie's venues), Pennsylvania (Presque Isle Downs, Lady Luck Nemacolin), New York (del Lago Resort), Louisiana (Fair Grounds), Mississippi (Harlow's Casino, Riverwalk Casino), Maine (Oxford Casino), Maryland (Ocean Downs), Florida (Calder Casino), Iowa (Hard Rock Sioux City), Indiana (Terre Haute under development), and New Hampshire (Chasers). The company also operates online wagering platforms serving customers in multiple states.
categories.supply_chain_position: Churchill Downs operates primarily in the downstream and direct-to-consumer segments of the gaming and entertainment supply chain. The company owns and operates gaming facilities, racetracks, and online wagering platforms that serve end consumers directly. The company also manufactures and operates pari-mutuel wagering systems through United Tote, positioning it as both a service provider and operator in the racing industry supply chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding historical racing machine (HRM) entertainment venues across multiple states, developing new casino resorts (Terre Haute, Dumfries, Emporia), enhancing Churchill Downs Racetrack through major capital projects (Homestretch Club, First Turn Experience, Paddock Project), growing the TwinSpires online wagering platform through partnerships with major sportsbooks (FanDuel, DraftKings), and pursuing strategic acquisitions to expand geographic footprint and gaming offerings. The company is also focused on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) initiatives including responsible gaming, energy efficiency, and diversity initiatives.
categories.revenue_model: Churchill Downs generates revenue through multiple streams: pari-mutuel wagering commissions on live and historical horse races, simulcast fees, advance deposit wagering (ADW) fees, casino gaming revenue from slot machines and table games, hotel services, food and beverage operations, admissions and event-related services, sponsorships and television rights, and technology services provided to third parties. The company also earns revenue from retail sportsbooks at gaming properties and through market access agreements with online sportsbooks.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Churchill Downs competes with traditional and Native American casinos, other racetracks, video lottery terminals, state-sponsored lotteries, online gaming platforms, sports betting operators (including DraftKings and FanDuel), and other forms of legalized gaming. The company is positioned as a leading operator in horse racing with the iconic Kentucky Derby and one of the largest online horse racing wagering platforms. It faces increasing competition from expanded gaming jurisdictions and new market entrants in sports betting and online gaming.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Churchill Downs is a large-cap gaming and entertainment company with 2022 net revenue of $1.81 billion (up 13% from 2021), net income of $439.4 million (up 76%), and Adjusted EBITDA of $763.6 million (up 22%). The company has total assets of $6.2 billion and total debt of $4.6 billion as of December 31, 2022. The company demonstrates strong growth trajectory with significant capital investments in new venues and expansions, generating substantial operating cash flow of $510.8 million in 2022.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Churchill Downs differentiates itself through ownership of the iconic Kentucky Derby, one of the longest continuously held annual sporting events in the U.S. with global appeal and premium sponsorship opportunities. The company offers integrated entertainment experiences combining live horse racing, historical racing machines, casino gaming, and online wagering through a single platform (TwinSpires). Key differentiators include state-of-the-art facilities, strong brand heritage, diversified geographic presence, and strategic partnerships with major sportsbooks to provide seamless multi-product wagering experiences to customers.
